blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Regrets his Exchange of Words with Hadhrat Umar (RA) and seeks Forgiveness

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came in (in a hurry) holding the edge of his clothing (and without him realising it) because of which his knees were exposed. Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "Look! Your friend has had an argument." After greeting with Salaam, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I had an argument with (Hadhrat Umar) Ibn Khattaab and in the heat of the discussion I told him something. I then regretted the words and asked him to forgive me. However, he refused to do so and I have therefore come to you." Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice repeated, "May Allaah forgive you, O Abu Bakr."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) later regretted (not forgiving Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) and went to his house. When he asked if Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was at home, he was informed that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was not there. He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and greeted with Salaam. However, Rasulullaah ﷺ's face reddened (with anger) so much that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) became alarmed. Kneeling down before Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) pleaded, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I swear by Allaah that it was I who was at fault." After Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had repeated this twice, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When Allaah sent me (as a Nabi) to you people, you all said that I was lying except for Abu Bakr who said, 'He is speaking the truth.' He then supported me with his health and wealth, so will you people not leave my companion alone for my sake?" This Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated twice, after which no one hurt Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) ever again. [^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once used insulting words for Hadhrat Umar (RA) but then said, "Please forgive me, dear brother." However, Hadhrat Umar (RA) was extremely angry (and refused to forgive him). Despite the fact that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) repeated his request several times, Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s anger did not abate. The incident was then reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ and when the Sahabah (RA) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and sat before him, he said, "Your brother asked you to forgive him but you failed to do so." Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "I swear by the Being Who has sent you with truth! There was not a time that he asked me to forgive him when I did not do so (privately). After yourself there is none of creation whom I like more than him." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then added, "And I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that after yourself there is none of creation whom I like more than him." Bukhaari, as quoted in Sifatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.92).
